Key facts As of 12 November 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), where community transmission is ongoing, has reported a total of 11 197 confirmed cases, including 5 471 related deaths (from data up until 11 November). Since the beginning of the outbreak, eight provinces have been affected: Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Tshopo, Haut-Uélé, Bas-Uélé, Sud Ubangi and Nord Ubangi. In Nigeria, one Ebola case was reported on 20 October 2026. The person has since been medically evacuated to Switzerland. The individual, who had travel history to Uganda, developed symptoms on 7 October, sought medical care on 11 October, and tested positive on 20 October. A total of 62 contacts of the case have been identified. In Kenya, a total of nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, have been reported, all linked to the first case. The last case was reported on 20 October 2026 and the second death was reported on 23 October 2026. As of 11 November, seven cases had recovered and all identified contacts under monitoring completed 21 days of quarantine. ECDC is monitoring the outbreak through its epidemic intelligence activities and actively liaising with partners to support the response. For more detailed epidemiological information and updates on the outbreak, visit ECDC’s Public health events page. Cases medically evacuated or imported to Europe Since May 2026, four cases of Ebola disease linked to the outbreak in DRC have been medically evacuated or imported to the European Union/European Economic Area (EU/EEA). Three patients were medically evacuated for specialised care, two to Germany and one to the Netherlands . A fourth case was reported in France in July. All four cases involved people working in healthcare or humanitarian roles in affected areas of DRC. In July, a resident of the United Kingdom (UK) was also evacuated to the UK following potential exposure while treating Ebola patients in DRC. On 26 October, a case reported in Nigeria and a close contact of hers were medically evacuated to Switzerland. ECDC risk assessment On the basis of the available information, and given the uncertainties surrounding this outbreak, the likelihood of infection for people from the European Union/European Economic Area (EU/EEA) living in or travelling to affected areas is estimated to be low. Given the very low likelihood of importation and secondary transmission, the likelihood of infection for people living in the EU/EEA is estimated to be very low. This assessment will be reviewed as further information becomes available.
